This is the view chosen by Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, Abū Ṣāliḥ and a group of the exegetes. ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās said: they are the horses of the warriors. This is the view of the companions of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan and a group, and it was chosen by al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj.

The proponents of the camels said: the sura is Meccan, and there was no jihad then, nor horses engaged in jihad. Rather, He swore by what they know and are familiar with, namely the camels of the pilgrims when they race from ʿArafa to Muzdalifa; thus they are ʿādiyāt. Ḍabḥ and ḍabʿ mean the camel's stretching of her flank in travel; it is said ḍabaḥat and ḍabaʿat with the same meaning. Abū ʿUbayda, who himself chose this view, recited:

"So there was for you my reward entirely, and the stout, broad-chested camel became panting amid the mirage."

They said: they race panting, and so they strike sparks with their hooves from the rubbing of stones against one another, and they raise dust (naqʿ), which is the dust of their running, and so they arrive in the middle of a gathering (jamʿ), which is Muzdalifa.

They said: horses are the ones that pant in their running; it is a sound heard from within their bellies, not a neigh nor a snort, but the sound of their breaths within them from the intensity of the running. Al-Jurjānī said: both views have been reported in the exegesis, but the context indicates that they are horses, namely His saying ﴿fal-muriyati qadhan﴾, and striking sparks (īrāʾ) occurs only with the hoof because of its hardness, whereas the camel's foot has softness and looseness. They said: ḍabḥ is more apparent in horses than in camels, and striking sparks is clearer with the hooves of horses than with the soft feet of camels. They said: naqʿ is dust, and the horses' stirring of dust by their running is more apparent than the stirring by camels' feet. The pronoun in "bihi" refers to the place in which they run. They said: the greatest stirring of dust at a raid is when the horses penetrate the middle of the enemy gathering in running, because of the great movement and turmoil in that place. As for interpreting the verse as referring to the stirring of dust in the valley of Muḥassar at the raid, this is not clear, and dust does not usually rise there because the ground is hard. This is among the greatest signs of the Lord, exalted is He, and proofs of His power and wisdom. So He reminds them of a blessing upon them in the creation of this animal, through which they gain victory over their enemies and attain their vengeance, just as He reminded them of His blessings upon them in the creation of camels, which carry their burdens from land to land. Camels are especially for carrying loads, and horses are especially for supporting men; so He reminds them of His blessings in both. When the proponents of the camels realized that the camel's feet are the furthest thing from striking fire, they interpreted the verse in distant ways. Weaker still is what is reported from him by Mujāhid: they are the thoughts of men that kindle the fire of deceit and trickery in war. And Allah knows best.

This is the matter of the oath.

And he said in (al-Furūsiyya):

The meaning of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Wal-ʿādiyāti ḍabḥan﴾:

The thirteenth: Allah, glorified is He, swore by horses in His Book, and that indicates their nobility and excellence with Him. He, exalted is He, said:

﴿By the racers, panting, then the strikers of sparks, then the raiders at dawn﴾ [al-ʿĀdiyāt: 1-3].

He swore, glorified is He, by horses that run in His way; ḍabḥ is a sound within their bellies as they run.

﴿Then the strikers of sparks﴾: they strike fire with their hooves when they strike the stone.

﴿Then raise thereby dust (naqʿan)﴾: naqʿ is the dust that horses raise in their running.

The pronoun in "bihi" is said to refer to the qadḥ, but this is weak, for dust is not raised by striking. It is said to refer to the raid (maghār), indicated by His saying ﴿fal-mughīrāt﴾, meaning they raised dust by the raid because of the abundance of their circling in it. It may refer to the raid, which is a verbal noun, meaning they raised dust because of the raiding. It may refer to the enemy understood from the word ﴿ʿādiyāt﴾.

The pronoun in the second "wa-bihi" is like the first. It is said to refer to the dust (naqʿ), meaning they penetrated the gathering (jamʿ) while mingled with dust; on this view "jamʿ" here means the enemy's gathering, and this is the saying of Ibn Masʿūd.

The first view is more preponderant for several reasons:

The first: ḍabḥ is used in reference to horses; this is why the people of the language said ḍabḥ is the sound of horses' breaths when they run. Allah, exalted is He, said ﴿Wal-ʿādiyāti ḍabḥan﴾. It is also said that a fox "ḍabaḥa."

The second: He described them as striking fire from stones as they run, and this is witnessed in horses, from the clanging of their hooves on the hard rock, so that the spark of fire is produced between them just as it is produced from iron and flint when struck.

The third: He described them as raiding. Although this word is also used for camels, as the Quraysh used to say, "We have entered upon Thabīr, so that we may raid," still its use for raiding in warfare is more common.

The fourth: He, glorified is He, related the raid to dawn, and the pilgrims at dawn do not raid, but are at the standing place of Muzdalifa; and the Quraysh at that time did not raid until the sun rose, so neither the Quraysh nor any other Arabs raided at dawn.

In the Ṣaḥīḥ, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he, in warfare, would not raid until dawn broke; and if he heard a call to prayer he refrained, and otherwise he raided.

The fifth: He, glorified is He, joined the penetration of the gathering with the fāʾ which denotes sequence after the raid. This requires that they raided at the time of dawn and then penetrated the gathering after the raid. It is known that the camels of the pilgrims have two raids: a raid at the beginning of the night toward a gathering, and a raid before sunrise from there toward Mina. The first raid is before dawn, and it is not possible to combine it with the time of dawn and with penetrating a gathering; this is evident.

The sixth: naqʿ is dust, and the gathering of Muzdalifa and all around it is stone (ṣafā), a valley between two mountains, in which there is no dust that camels could raise.

And Allah knows best what He meant by His speech.

And he said in (al-Furūsiyya):

The meaning of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Wal-ʿādiyāti ḍabḥan﴾:

He swore, glorified is He, by horses that run in His way; ḍabḥ is a sound within their bellies as they run.

**(Section)**

It was also said: the land that produces nothing of benefit. Al-Fadl ibn 'Abbas said: the *kanud* is one whom a single act of wrongdoing makes forget many acts of goodness.

If this wrongdoing ignorant one knew that he is the one who sits on the path of his own interests, cutting them off from reaching him, that he is the stone in the path of the water on which his life depends, and that he is the blockage that has closed the channel of water to the garden of his heart, and yet he cries out, "Thirst! Thirst!", while he himself has stood in the path of the water and prevented its reaching him, then he is the veil of his heart from the secret of its unseen, and the cloud that blocks the rising of the sun of guidance upon the heart. Nothing is more harmful to him than himself, and he has no enemies more effective in harming him and in hostility toward him than himself.

*What enemies can inflict upon an ignorant man / is not as much as the ignorant man inflicts upon himself.*

So woe to him, a wrongdoer in the form of one wronged, complaining while the fault is his own. He has striven in turning away, while he cries out, "They have expelled me and distanced me!" He turned his back to the door, indeed he locked it upon himself, lost its keys and broke them, and he says:

*He called me, then closed the door before me, so is there any way / for my entry? Make my case clear to me.*

The compassionate one takes him by his waistband away from the fire, while he pulls against him, tears his garment, overpowers him and plunges into it, crying out, "What can I do? They have brought me forward to the pit and thrown me into it!" By Allah, how often the advisor has cried out to him, "Beware! Beware! Keep away! Keep away!" How often he has held his garment, and how often he has shown him the corpses of those who plunged in, yet he refuses anything but plunging:

*How many advices have I offered for your sake, / though the sincere advisor may earn suspicion.*

Woe to him! He is a helper of Satan against his Lord, an adversary of Allah within his own self, compelled in sins and free-willed in obedience, weak in judgment, a squanderer of his opportunity, sitting idle from his interests, blaming the decrees of his Lord, arguing against his Lord with what He would not accept from His servant, his wife or his slave-girl if they argued with it against him in neglecting some of his command. If he commanded one of them to do something and they neglected it, or forbade them something and they committed it, and said, "Destiny drove me to that," he would not accept this argument from them, and would hasten to punish them.

If destiny is an argument for you, O wrongdoing ignorant one, in abandoning the right of your Lord, then why would it not be an argument for your servant and slave-girl in abandoning some of your right? Rather, if a wrongdoer harms you and a transgressor assaults you and argues by destiny, your anger would intensify against him, his offense would be multiplied in your eyes, and you would see his argument as refuted. Then you argue with it before your Lord and see it as an excuse for yourself! Who is more deserving of injustice and ignorance than one in this state?

This is in addition to the continuous kindness of Allah to you with every breath: He removed your ailments, enabled you to gather provision for His paradise, sent you the guide, relieved you of the burden of travel and of what you need for it, and what you use to fight the highwaymen who attack you. He gave you hearing, sight and heart, made you know good and evil, the beneficial and the harmful.

He sent His Messenger to you, sent down His Book to you, made it easy for remembrance, understanding and action, and aided you with reinforcements from His noble soldiers, who strengthen you and guard you, fight your enemy and drive him away from you, and desire that you not incline toward him or make peace with him, while they spare you his harm. Yet you refuse anything but supporting him against them and befriending him rather than them, indeed supporting and befriending him instead of your true Ally, who is more deserving of you. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," they prostrated, except Iblis; he was of the jinn and defied the command of his Lord. Will you then take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me while they are an enemy to you? Evil is the exchange for the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Kahf: 50]. He expelled Iblis from His heaven, removed him from His paradise, and distanced him from His nearness, when he did not prostrate to you while you were in the loins of your father Adam, because of your honor with Him. So he (Iblis) took enmity toward you and distanced himself. Then you befriended his enemy, inclined to him, and made peace with him, and yet you wrong yourself and complain of expulsion and distance, saying:

*They accustomed me to union, and union is sweet, / then they threw me into aversion, and aversion is harsh.*

Yes, and how could one expelled by such treatment not be expelled? How could one who is so described not be distanced? How could one whose conduct is thus make himself among the intimates and the close ones of Him? He has corrupted and clouded what is between him and Allah.

Allah commanded him to give thanks to Him, not because He needs it, but so that he may obtain more of His bounty. Thus He made ingratitude for His blessings, and using them to disobey Him, among the greatest causes of their being withdrawn from him.

He commanded him to remember Him so that He would remind him of His kindness, so He made his forgetting a cause of Allah's forgetting him: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves﴾ [al-Hashr: 19], ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [al-Tawba: 67]. He commanded him to ask Him so that He would give him, but he did not ask Him, yet He gave him the most excellent gifts without asking, and he did not accept them. He complains to one who has mercy on him to one who has no mercy on him, and feels wronged by one who does not wrong him, and leaves the one who is hostile to him and wrongs him. If Allah grants him health, well-being, wealth and status, he uses these blessings to disobey Him, and if He takes these from him, he remains displeased with his Lord while complaining of Him. He is not fit for well-being, nor for trial: well-being casts him into what angers Allah, and trial drives him to disbelief in the blessing and denial of its favor, and to complaining to His creatures.

He called him to His door, but he did not stand at it nor knock upon it. Then He opened it for him, but he did not turn toward it nor enter it. He sent His Messenger to him, calling him to the abode of His honor, but he disobeyed the Messenger and said, "I do not sell the present for the absent, or cash for credit, nor do I abandon what I see for something I have heard of," and he says:

*Take what you see and leave what you have heard of, / in the sunrise there is what suffices you from Saturn.*

If obeying the Messenger happens to coincide with his interest, he obeys in order to attain his interest, not out of pleasure in the one who sent him. He keeps hating Him through his sins until He turns away from him and shuts the door in his face.

Yet with all this, He does not despair him of His mercy, but says: "Whenever you come to Me, I accept you. If you come to Me at night, I accept you; if you come to Me by day, I accept you. If you draw near to Me a span, I draw near to you a cubit; if you draw near to Me a cubit, I draw near to you a fathom; if you walk toward Me, I run toward you. If you meet Me with the earth's fullness of sins, then meet Me without associating anything with Me, I will come to you with its fullness of forgiveness. Even if your sins reach the clouds of heaven, then you ask My forgiveness, I will forgive you. Who is greater than Me in generosity and bounty?

My servants fight Me with great sins, while I protect them in their beds. Indeed I and the jinn and mankind are in a great matter: I create and others are worshipped; I provide and others are thanked. My good descends upon the servants, while their evil ascends to Me. I make Myself beloved to them with My blessings, while I am independent of them, and they hate Me through sins, while they are the neediest of things to Me.

Whoever comes to Me, I meet him from afar; whoever turns away from Me, I call him from near. Whoever leaves something for My sake, I give him more than he hopes. Whoever desires My pleasure, I make him desire what I desire. Whoever acts by My power and strength, I make iron soft for him.

The people of My remembrance are the people of My company; the people of My thanks are the people of My increase; the people of My obedience are the people of My honor; and the people of My disobedience, I will not despair them of My mercy. If they repent to Me, I am their beloved, for I love those who repent and I love those who purify themselves. If they do not repent to Me, I am their physician: I afflict them with calamities to purify them of their faults."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 100, verse 9–11:

Then He, glorified is He, warns the human being who has this description, when He scatters what is in the graves and obtains what is in the breasts. That is: He distinguishes, gathers, makes clear, manifests, and the like. And He, glorified is He, combined the graves and the breasts, just as the Prophet (ﷺ) combined them in his saying: "May Allah fill their bellies and their graves with fire." For a person conceals in his breast what is in it of good and evil, and he conceals in his grave his body. So the Lord brings out his body from his grave and his secret from his breast, so his body becomes exposed upon the earth and his secret becomes apparent on his face, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾

And He said: ﴿We will mark him upon the snout﴾.

(Section)

The object of knowledge, if you read it "inna" with a kasra, is because of the lam. He, glorified is He, specified His being Acquainted with them on that Day, though He is Acquainted with them at every time, as a notice of the recompense, and that He will recompense them on that Day according to what He knows of them. So He mentioned knowledge while meaning its consequence. And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best.

(Subtle point)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, their Lord, about them, on that Day, is Acquainted﴾. He made it absolute in the rest of them, looking to the fact that the origin of His being Most Knowledgeable of them is established in both abodes.
